messages:
priya (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the tool-calling / structured-output work for the next sprint. customer asks piling up, want a clear PRD + acceptance checklist.
omar (eng): +1. Are we focusing on schema validation + graceful fallback only, or full function routing/authorization too?
priya (PM): MVP = schema validation, typed error responses, and a simple fallback policy (retry -> default-output -> human-alert). Auth/rbac routing is next quarter.
liz (eng): For validation, do we want server-side JSON Schema v7 or a custom lightweight validator? JSON Schema covers most cases but is heavy for streaming.
sam (design): Designers want predictable shape for the UI. If validation fails, we need a stable partial payload shape so clients can render a fallback card.
tess (cs): Top customers want explicit error codes so they can programmatically detect contract breaks. Example: `ERR_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD`, `ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH`, `ERR_CONTRADICTION`.
evan (sre): We also need observability hooks — per-request schema outcome + latency bucket, and a flag for fallback-used. Rollout depends on metrics.
priya (PM): Acceptance criteria proposal (high level):
- 95% of validated calls return either valid output or one of the defined error codes.
- Clear, documented fallback behavior for invalid outputs.
- Telemetry: schema_result, validation_errors, fallback_used present in traces.
- Backwards compatible: old clients shouldn't break.
sam (design): Add UX acceptance: fallback card shows reason (human-friendly) and a link to raw output for debugging.
omar (eng): Implementation notes: we'll add validation as a post-generation step before response commit. If invalid -> run deterministic sanitizer -> if still invalid -> emit error code + fallback payload.
liz (eng): Example validator behavior (pseudo):
```
validate(output, schema) -> {
  if valid: return {status: OK, payload}
  if fixable: return {status: SANITIZED, payload: sanitized}
  else: return {status: ERROR, code: ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, details: [..]}
}
```
priya (PM): Edge cases to call out in PRD: nested optional arrays, polymorphic union types, streaming partials, and tool-call side effects (idempotency).
tess (cs): Also include clear guidance for when customers should opt into strict mode vs permissive. We have some customers who want hard errors.
evan (sre): Rollout plan suggestion: alpha internal -> 10% canary on hosted -> monitor (errors, fallbacks, latency) -> 100% with opt-out for Dedicated customers.
omar (eng): For streaming, we can validate only final committed JSON (after closing tokens) and keep latency impact minimal. But for early client-side streaming render we should provide an optional `schema_preview` hook.
sam (design): Can we provide a standard fallback payload template? e.g., { "_fallback": true, "reason": "string", "raw": "string" }
liz (eng): Agree. Also need de-dup of errors in details to avoid massive logs. Limit to top 5 errors per request.
priya (PM): Draft acceptance checklist to include in PRD:
- Schema spec documented with examples.
- Validator behavior documented (OK/SANITIZED/ERROR codes).
- Fallback payload and UX template included.
- Telemetry names & dashboards created.
- Rollout plan & canary thresholds (error rate <0.5%, fallback_used <1%).
- Backwards compat compatibility notes.
tess (cs): I'll add a customer-impact table: which customers need strict mode, recommended timeline for outreach.
evan (sre): Canary thresholds seem OK, add SLO guardrails for 99th percentile latency increase <100ms.
omar (eng): One more technical edge: validate function call arguments separately and ensure we never execute a tool if validation fails unless customer explicitly allows. Important for safety.
priya (PM): Good call. We'll make default: no tool execution on validation error. Add an opt-in flag: `execute_on_invalid:true` for power customers with disclaimers.
sam (design): UX should hide raw flags unless `debug=true`. Keep default surface clean.
priya (PM): Next steps: Omar + Liz draft the PRD sections (requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases) by EOW. Tess will map customers for strict-mode. Evan will draft rollout and observability plan. Sam will supply fallback template. I'll consolidate and circulate for RFC review.
omar (eng): Will do. I'll add a small JSON Schema example to the PRD for the address-case.
liz (eng): Also propose a short set of unit tests and an integration harness for customer sample prompts.
engbot: Reminder: PRD doc created: /docs/prd/toolchain-structured-output-1812345678-draft.md
priya (PM): Thanks all — ping here if anything blocks EOW. :thumbsup:
